ideas.title: Ham Radio Turns 100 in Austria: What That Milestone Means for All of Us
ideas.why_now: The OEVSV is celebrating its centennial this week, with IARU Region 1 board meeting in Vienna right now.
ideas.angle: Use the anniversary as a jumping-off point to talk about why clubs matter, how the hobby has changed over 100 years, and what everyday hams can take from that history.

ideas.title: Remembering Doug KI6DS: Why the QRP Kit World Owes Him a Lot
ideas.why_now: KI6DS was announced as a Silent Key this week, generating tributes across the ham radio community.
ideas.angle: Tell the story of CalQRP and its classic kits for listeners who may not know the name, and connect it to why kit building culture still thrives today.

ideas.title: SSTV in 2026: Sending Pictures Over Radio Is Easier Than You Think
ideas.why_now: SSTV activity on 20 meters is visibly up this week, and a new Android and iOS app with logging just launched.
ideas.angle: Walk a curious beginner through what SSTV actually sounds and looks like, what gear or software you need, and how to make your first contact.

ideas.title: WSPR With Junk From the Garage: What Everyday Objects Make Good Antennas
ideas.why_now: A Canadian Amateur article on backyard WSPR tests with ladders, gutters, and shovels sparked laughs and genuine curiosity this week.
ideas.angle: Replicate the spirit of the experiment on the show. Discuss WSPR as a low-effort propagation tool and inspire listeners to try weird antennas from around the house.

ideas.title: China Restricts APRS and WSPR: What Is Actually Happening
ideas.why_now: A report circulating this week says Chinese authorities are cracking down on APRS and WSPR use by amateur operators.
ideas.angle: Explain what APRS and WSPR actually do, why governments might view them as a concern, and what it means for the global ham community without sensationalizing.

sources.label: Mastodon #amateurradio, China APRS and WSPR crackdown

ideas.title: The Quansheng UV-K5 SSB Mod: Should You Actually Do It
ideas.why_now: SSB is one of the top trending terms this week, and a QRP Quarterly article on the UV-K5 SSB mod is getting fresh attention from HT owners.
ideas.angle: Break down what the mod does, how hard it is, and whether it delivers real utility or is mostly a fun experiment. Perfect for listeners who already own one of these radios.

ideas.title: Power Line Noise: Five Months to Fix It, and How It Finally Got Done
ideas.why_now: Multiple operators posted this week about RFI victories and ongoing interference battles, keeping the topic active in the community.
ideas.angle: Walk through the practical steps one ham took to get the utility company to act, and give listeners a realistic playbook for their own RFI fights.

ideas.title: Old CB Radios as Parts Donors: The Budget Builder's Secret Weapon
ideas.why_now: A tip about harvesting finals from CB radios for DIY transmitters drew genuine interest in the community this week.
ideas.angle: Practical and fun for any builder. Discuss what parts are worth pulling, where to find cheap CB radios, and how this fits into a broader scrappy builder philosophy.
